chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Mr. Spooner, Glaudius Marshall and the St. Marks brass band
summary: Spooner takes him to Glaudius Marshall, choirmaster of St. Marks, who sends him to the Martin Smith School and into the church brass band after a sight-reading test.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yes, and Mr. -- what's his name, Mr. Spooner, he was a famous pianist,
Briggs

we had a conversation and I told him about my musical background. He was very surprised that, you know --. He said, 'Well, look, you're a kid, and I can take you to someone who could probably help you to continue your studies.'
So he took me to Mr. Glaudius Marshall, who was a choirmaster, organist and conductor of the St. Marks 138th Street -- What do you call it -- Brass Band.
The church had a brass band?
Yes, yes, yes. We all had a brass band.
The churches all had brass bands?
Oh yes.
What was that, to keep the kids out of trouble sort of --
I guess it must have been something about it, 'cause it was an awfully nice thing.
After meeting Mr. Glaudius Marshall
Briggs
who introduced me to the Martin Smith School -- do you remember Martin Smith?
No, I don't know that either.
You're too young.
Right.

(Laughter). Yes, well, he take me to the Martin Smith School and in the meanwhile, as he was in charge of the brass band, I became affiliated with the brass band. He said, 'Come on, Arthur,' you know.
And after testing my sight reading and everything, I became a member as a kid.
You played coronet?
Oh, yes.
